articles.title: Rugby League World Cup 2030 to be staged in Pacific-USA with eligibility rules updated and Tonga, Samoa given Tier 1 status
articles.summary: It has been proposed that Tonga and Samoa will be given Tier 1 status thanks to their on-field performances; the RLWC 2030 will take place across the Pacific and USA; it will have a 'Magic Round' format that will see the tournament descend on a new host city each week
articles.body:
The competitions will be played with a 'Magic Round' format that will see the teams arrive in a host city for a round of the tournaments before moving on.

The IRL board has also approved changes to international eligibility rules to increase the pool of players available to nations and they have endorsed the elevation of Tonga and Samoa to Men's Tier 1 status, subject to consultation with both teams.

The elevation of Samoa and Tonga as Tier 1 nations would be in recognition of their performances on and off the field, with both nations reaching the semi-finals of RLWC26. Samoa became the first Pacific nation to play in a World Cup final in 2022, while Tonga are the only Tier 2 nation to have defeated Australia, England and New Zealand.

The IRL board has also agreed to extend the eligibility criteria for players to be eligible to represent their nation of heritage if either they, a parent, a grandparent or a great grandparent were born there, the great grandparent element being added.

The decision comes off the back of a submission from Cook Islands given their small population of less than 20,000 and the movement of Cook Islanders to larger countries for work, study or other purposes.

The wheelchair tournament looks set to be hosted in France at the same time, while the men's tournament will increase from 10 to 12 teams, with the women's increasing from eight to 10.

IRL chair Troy Grant said: "The IRL board has decided that the next Rugby League World Cup for men and women in 2030 will be staged in the Pacific-USA. The next Wheelchair World Cup is going to be run at the same time in France.

"This is a strategy to maximise the interest of broadcasters, government partners and fans in the current World Cup, which has regularly broken records for crowds and the number of television viewers because of the outstanding skill, intensity and passion of the players and teams.

"At the same time we want to take advantage of opportunities that are opening up in new frontiers where the Rugby League World Cup hasn't previously been played.

"The World Cup under its current format runs for five weeks and RLWC30 is going to be run in five locations across the Pacific and USA. We haven't decided where yet; we are going to market and will look at the strategic placement of which cities we go to.

"The cities will be ones that have the appropriate stadia to run matches over multiple days to get all of the pool matches played in one location.

"This will be similar to a Magic Round, so IRL Rugby League World Cup 2030 will arrive in town, the stadium will be activated and there will be a lot of opportunities to promote the teams and the game. The World Cup will then move to the next city that is identified.

"There are three weeks where every nation is involved and then we have semi-finals and finals.

"The format for what that will look like is yet to be decided and nations were asked for feedback during the IRL AGM and Congress in Sydney over the weekend."

The IRL board has also proposed that the 2034 Rugby League World Cup be played under a similar format in Europe, coinciding with the 100th anniversary of the game in France, which was behind the establishment of the World Cup in 1954.

articles.title: Ireland rugby: Sean Jansen ruled out of Fiji and South Africa games with knee injury
articles.summary: Sean Jansen is ruled out of the remainder of Ireland's Nations Championship campaign with a knee injury, further depleting head coach Andy Farrell's options at number eight.
articles.body:
Sean Jansen has been ruled out of the remainder of Ireland's Nations Championship campaign with a knee injury, further depleting head coach Andy Farrell's options at number eight.

With Caelan Doris and Jack Conan already injured, Jansen was forced off during Friday's 42-12 win over Argentina in Dublin and will return to Connacht to continue his rehabilitation.

Hooker Dan Sheehan will miss Saturday's home match with Fiji (20:10 GMT) after sustaining a concussion against the Pumas, but the coaching staff are "hopeful" wing Rob Baloucoune (cramp) and flanker Josh van der Flier (ankle) will be available.

Sheehan - squad captain in Doris' absence - is a doubt for the South Africa game on 21 November as he undergoes 12-day return-to-play protocols.

With mounting back-row injury issues, uncapped Ulster forward David McCann has been called up, while Gus McCarthy has joined the squad to boost Farrell's options at hooker.

Centre Bundee Aki, a late withdrawal from the Argentina game with illness, is expected to resume full training on Tuesday.

After facing Fiji and back-to-back world champions South Africa at Aviva Stadium, Ireland will travel to Twickenham for a finals weekend fixture.

McCann and McCarthy were originally named in the Ireland XV squad for their fixture against Fiji 'A' in Cork on 20 November.

Tom Ahern (neck), Ethan McIlroy (thumb) and Michael Milne (ankle) have all been ruled out of the XV game, with Fineen Wycherley, Todd Lawlor and Jeremy Loughman called up.

articles.title: Nations Championship: England's Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and Tom Curry ruled out of rest of tournament
articles.summary: Steve Borthwick's side have been hit by a raft of injuries ahead of their Nations Championship clash against Japan; Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and Tom Curry have been ruled out of the autumn series
articles.body:
It comes as Steve Borthwick's side has been hit with a series of injuries ahead of their clash against Japan on Saturday.

Seb Atkinson, who came off in the second-half of England's 45-22 win against Australia, is set to miss the match with a hip injury, along with Ollie Chessum (shoulder) and George Furbank (groin).

England are optimistic the trio will be available for their clash against New Zealand at Allianz Stadium on Saturday, November 21.

Feyi-Waboso sustained an injury to his right ankle during the first-half of England's clash against the Wallabies, following a hip-drop tackle by Australia prop Angus Bell.

Bell was later sent to the sin bin, with Henry Pollock coming on to replace Feyi-Waboso on the wing at half-time. Pollock would go on to score twice.

The Exeter winger's absence could see Borthwick call on Saracens fliers Noah Caluori or Tobias Elliott for England's clash against Japan.

It would be Caluori's third cap for England, having made his senior debut during their Nations Championship clash against Fiji in July.

Centres Joe Marchant and Will Joseph could also be considered as wing options, while Fraser Dingwall or Max Ojomoh are likely to take the No 12 jersey in place of Atkinson.

Curry did not feature in England's win over Australia after he sustained a hip injury during training last week.

Borthwick revealed after Sunday's win that his brother, Ben Curry, was unlikely to start against Japan, despite the openside enjoying an excellent outing against the Wallabies.

It is likely Borthwick could deploy Freddie Steward at full-back in place of Furbank and keep Marcus Smith on the bench as utility cover.

England's 36-player squad returned to Pennyhill Park on Monday to prepare for this weekend's clash, with Jack Kenningham and Max Hicks both being drafted into the squad as back-row cover for Ben Curry and Chessum.

Meanwhile, Archie McParland has returned to the training squad after recovering from a calf injury.

Rehabilitation: Seb Atkinson (Gloucester Rugby), Ollie Chessum (Leicester Tigers), George Furbank (Harlequins)

articles.title: Immanuel Feyi-Waboso: England wing out of Nation Championship with ankle injury
articles.summary: England wing Immanuel Feyi-Waboso is ruled out of the rest of the Nations Championship as his injury misfortune continues.
articles.body:
England wing Immanuel Feyi-Waboso has been ruled out of the rest of the Nations Championship as his injury misfortune continues.

The 23-year-old injured his ankle in the first half of Sunday's 45-22 win over Australia in a "hip-drop" tackle by Angus Bell, for which the Wallabies prop received a yellow card.

England will also be without a handful of other key players for the match against Japan on Saturday, with Seb Atkinson, forward Ollie Chessum and full-back George Furbank all ruled out.

In a further blow, it has been confirmed experienced flanker Tom Curry will not feature this autumn after feeling discomfort in his hip.

Newcastle's uncapped flanker Max Hicks has been called into the 36-man squad, along with Harlequins' Jack Kenningham, while scrum-half Archie McParland, centre Max Ojomoh and wings Noah Calouri and Tobias Elliott are also included.

After hosting the Brave Blossoms in Twickenham, England face the in-form New Zealand All Blacks at Allianz Stadium on Saturday, 21 November.

The finals weekend takes place between 27-29 November.

England make massive step up in Australia victory

England swat aside Wallabies to back up Borthwick

Injuries take gloss off dominant display

Monday's injury update has taken the gloss off an exceptional England display against Australia, as Steve Borthwick's side produced their best performance of the year in a seven-try humbling of the Wallabies.

After bursting on to the international scene at the start of 2024, Feyi-Waboso has established himself as an X-factor talent but has been beset by injuries.

He missed the Six Nations in 2025 after undergoing shoulder surgery and was absent from this year's edition with a hamstring injury.

Feyi-Waboso was one of England's best players in the July leg of the Nations Championship, and had recovered from a hamstring problem picked up on club duty to start against Australia in a potent back three with Furbank and Tommy Freeman.

But Feyi-Waboso suffered his latest injury in the 32nd minute after the tackle by Bell and was replaced on the wing by Henry Pollock, normally a back row, after half-time.

Meanwhile, with Atkinson absent with a hip problem, Borthwick will need to field a new centre combination, meaning Fraser Dingwall or Max Ojomoh are in line to play at inside-centre.

At full-back, Furbank produced a consummate performance in his first England game in two years, but now will miss at least the Japan match because of a groin niggle.

It is hoped Atkinson and Furbank - as well as vice-captain Chessum, who has a shoulder injury - will all be available to face the All Blacks in 12 days' time.
